modifications: Entries were selected, normalised (HTML removed, years parsed, headline titles shortened to about 100 characters with an ellipsis), merged and de-duplicated across sources, ranked, capped per day and category, and sorted. Summaries keep the source wording. did_you_know facts are either Wikipedia "Did you know" hooks (text only, reformatted) or one-sentence rewordings of existing entries (prefixed with the date, possibly shortened). Image links are unmodified Wikimedia URLs.

did_you_know.fact: On July 5, 1980: Swedish tennis player Björn Borg wins his fifth Wimbledon final and becomes the first male tennis player to win the championships five times in a row (1976–1980).

On July 5, 1977: The Pakistan Armed Forces under Muhammad Zia-ul-Haq seize power in Operation Fair Play and begin 11 years of martial law. Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, the first elected Prime Minister of Pakistan, is overthrown.
On July 5, 1954: Elvis Presley recorded his first single, "That's All Right", at Sun Records in Memphis, Tennessee.

image_credit.author: Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer, Inc. Reproduction Number: LC-USZ6-2067 Location: NYWTS -- BIOG

did_you_know.fact: July 5 is observed as Fifth of July (New York), historic celebration of the abolition of slavery in New York in 1827.
July 5 is observed as Tynwald Day, if July 5 is on a weekend, the holiday is the following Monday. (Isle of Man).
